comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth segment business definition and scope
comparisons.peer_summary: The Wealth segment comprises the Private Bank, Wealth at Work, and Citigold businesses, providing financial services such as banking, lending, and custody to affluent, high net worth, and ultra-high net worth clients across 20 countries including the U.S., Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE, and London.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Citi provide a structural overview of their wealth management businesses, but focus on different aspects. BAC's GWIM overview focuses on the aggregate client balance size and the breadth of the product suite (investment, brokerage, banking, trust, retirement). Citi's Wealth segment disclosure focuses on the internal composition of the segment (Private Bank, Wealth at Work, Citigold) and the specific client tiers served (affluent, high net worth, ultra-high net worth) across specific global locations.

sentences.text: Our GWIM businesses, with client balances of $4.3 trillion, provide tailored solutions to meet client needs through a full set of investment management, brokerage, banking, trust and retirement products.

Wealth includes the Private Bank, Wealth at Work and Citigold businesses and provides financial services to a range of client segments including affluent, high net worth and ultra-high net worth clients through banking, lending, mortgages, investment, custody and trust product offerings in 20 countries, including the U.S., Mexico and four wealth management centers: Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE and London.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth advisory and private banking services
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers tailored wealth advisory services to ultra-high-net-worth clients, personalized financial planning, and a full range of private banking services including deposits, loans, and securities execution, with deposits also raised through Marcus.
comparisons.comparison: While BAC and GS both operate wealth management divisions providing investment and private banking services, they differ in their stated scope and product emphasis. BAC's GWIM provides a 'full set' of products including trust and retirement products with a specific balance sheet metric ($4.3 trillion). GS specifically highlights tailored advisory services for 'ultra-high-net worth clients' and emphasizes its private banking services, including deposits raised through its Marcus platform, without providing a comparable aggregate client balance figure in this specific disclosure snippet.

In addition, we offer clients a full range of private banking services, including a variety of deposit alternatives and loans that our clients use to finance investments in both financial and nonfinancial assets, bridge cash flow timing gaps or provide liquidity and flexibility for other needs.
